title: Soil Thermal Conservation Contract

invariants.evidence: Adds a generic derived thermal-energy view to the existing single SWAP5 kernel/process architecture; no alternate SWAP implementation.
New production module contains no file, path, parser or I/O primitive dependency; gate checks this statically.
Energy coverage/result semantics are explicit derived data and are not mixed into parameters, forcing or physical state.
No persistent per-column physical state is added; the view is derived from an interval result.
No new scratch state is added. Existing F-PM07B worker workspace remains unchanged.
The view is compact and allocation-free, but EB-I02-R1 does not perform a large-batch cache/SIMD throughput qualification.
EB-I02-R1 does not mutate committed state or introduce an alternate transaction mechanism. Existing F-MR39/F-CI45 atomic water+thermal transaction authority is preserved byte-for-byte.
No committed state is modified by the derived view; existing rollback/retry/warm-start behavior is unchanged.
The view is explicitly defined over generic finite [t0,t1]; no day/month/year assumption.
No coupling-window duration or midnight/calendar boundary is encoded.
The conservation-ready view is suitable for later runtime/coupler composition, but EB-I02-R1 does not wire it into coupling publication.
No SWAP-MODFLOW head/flux interface behavior is changed.
No water state, water flux, water mass ledger or mass residual is modified.
No groundwater response tangent is changed or added.
The derived view requires no additional SWAP solve or predictor/corrector run.
No mandatory column state or solver instance is added, but hundred-thousand-column throughput is not benchmarked here.
Energy units are per owning logical column/tile area. Tile fractions and MODFLOW-cell aggregation remain outside the process contract.
No deep-vadose component behavior is changed.
No transition between deep-vadose and direct groundwater coupling is changed.
The new view depends on the generic process hydraulic view and restricted thermal result, not on HeadCalc or one Richards internal implementation.
Existing independently qualified soil-temperature physics is reused byte-identically; no duplicate thermal physics is introduced.
No HeadCalc internals or hydraulic solver arrays are referenced.
No numerical policy changes physical options. Coverage flags describe accounted physics only.
The view itself is bounded small work, but EB-I02-R1 does not qualify pathological-column or full MultiSWAP runtime cost behavior.
F-VQ58 scientific oracle is replayed with the exact historical output hash; existing reference thermal behavior remains available.
Coverage and residual diagnostics are explicit, but runtime-wide diagnostic aggregation/reporting is deferred.
No optional physical state or heavy allocation is introduced for columns that do not request the view.
Area aggregation and system composition remain runtime/coupler responsibilities; the process view is column-local.
No .swp, file-format, midnight, one-day or mandatory-MODFLOW assumption is present.
EB-I02-R1 is explicitly assessed against all 30 SWAP core architecture invariants in this audit.

hard_nonclaims: No full physical energy balance is qualified.
Liquid-water advective enthalpy is not accounted.
Vapor transport energy is not accounted.
Freeze/thaw and other phase-change enthalpy are not accounted.
Surface Rn-H-LE-G closure is not accounted.
Constant water content is not treated as proof of zero advective energy flux.
EB-I01 ledger composition is not part of this workunit.
Large-batch MultiSWAP throughput and bounded-cost behavior are not qualified.
Independent verification and canonical admission are not claimed.
